note: Frozen artifact-selection contract for every external dependency of this Midnight 1.x demo. Each field was re-derived from a live source on the freeze date. scripts/verify-artifact-decisions.sh enforces it offline. Do not edit a digest, SHA or hash to make a build pass: re-verify against the source first, then regenerate pinsDigest with --update-pins so the change is visible in review. Schema v2 differs from the 2.x sibling's v1 by adding `sources` (git-pinned source builds) and `toolchains`, and by replacing the warehouse proof-data generation with a pre-warm strategy.
selectionRule: Prefer a good official multiarch OCI image pinned by index digest. Otherwise use the verified official warehouse binary inside a thin local image. Otherwise mirror an unreliable upstream OCI image exactly into an owner-controlled registry. Only build from source when no reusable executable artifact exists.

warehouse.warning: DEVELOPMENT ONLY - NOT FOR PRODUCTION USE. Release 0.3.120 is mutable; verify every downloaded SHA-256 against this file before installation or execution.

components.reason: A good official multiarch image exists for the exact required version. Repacking it under another registry owner would add risk and no value.

Unlike the 4.4.0-rc.3 the 2.x sibling needs, 4.3.3 IS published as a good official multiarch image, so this repository neither compiles it nor installs a warehouse binary into a thin local image. Both are strictly worse when an official index exists.
$comment: The index also carries two unknown/unknown attestation manifests (sha256:57b5182d… and
sha256:1452f338…), which are in-toto provenance attachments referencing the two real
platform manifests, not runnable platforms. They are deliberately NOT recorded as
platforms: `platforms` means 'what this stack may run', and an attestation manifest is
not that.
4.3.3 serves an IDENTICAL GraphQL schema at /api/v3/graphql and /api/v4/graphql. Both
paths are asserted by verify.sh so a future version that drops one cannot break half
the stack silently.

components.reason: A good official multiarch image exists for the ledger-v8 proof server. Nothing here compiles with --feature-zkir-v3, so no second variant, no separate pin, and no mirror record are needed.

The combined local Celestia devnet runtime is carried over unchanged in identity from midnight-2-offers: these two versions are exactly what @effectstream/celestia@0.103.1 — a kernel-main dependency — vendors, so this is the devnet the offer-files kernel was developed against. Both binaries come from the warehouse by TARGETARCH; Linux arm64 IS published, so there is no platform pin.

sources.role: the Midnight Intents relay and the phase1-native-swaps browser UI
sources.reason: The audited pin the PR #52 solver was proven against end to end. Recorded as an IDENTITY ONLY. The repository is private and this public repository carries none of its content, fetches it from nowhere, and deliberately has no repository URL here — an operator supplies their own clone through RELAY_SOURCE_DIR and up.sh verifies it sits at this exact commit with a clean tree before any build. verifiedOn is null on purpose: this executor made no attempt to read the private remote, so claiming a verification date would be a fabrication.
$comment: Every rule this pin implies is enforced mechanically, not by convention:
* .gitignore ignores local/, the conventional place for the operator's clone;
* scripts/verify-no-private-source.sh fails on any committed byte of that source;
* scripts/lib/common.sh assert_relay_source() verifies the clone before a build;
* images built from it are never pushed to any registry.
Bumping this pin requires re-running the P5 end-to-end driver — the solver pin above
was proven against THIS relay commit and no other.

toolchains.requiredBy: images/zswap-da — the frozen template's scripts/build-contract.ts pins COMPILER_VERSION 0.31.0 and its committed src/contract/manifest.json verifies all 16 outputs plus the source hash byte-for-byte
toolchains.reason: RESOLVED AT P3/T3.3 (Q9). This is not a version this repository chose: the frozen template DICTATES it. scripts/build-contract.ts pins COMPILER_VERSION = "0.31.0" and src/contract/manifest.json records the sha256 of the contract source (6fde5f8e2cfc5d5559f1468f3997f72810aec3093c6a87a54036b9175dadd3f0 — byte-identical to kernel main's copy) and of all 16 generated files; `compact compile` is deterministic, so any other compiler fails that manifest. The compiler is also the right partner for the template's runtime pins: compact-runtime 0.16.0 / compact-js 2.5.1 / midnight-js 4.1.1, which the Midnight Preview matrix pairs with the Compact 0.31.x toolchain. Q9's original option table was enumerated against LFDT-Minokawa/compact and assumed a 0.30.0 pin was needed; both premises were wrong — see `compact-kernel` for the other half of the split. The asset is fetched and sha256-verified in the image rather than through the `compact` version manager, whose resolution is an unpinnable network lookup.
$comment: TWO COMPACT TOOLCHAINS, ON PURPOSE. This entry is the FRONTEND half (0.31.0, images/
zswap-da); `compact-kernel` is the kernel half (0.30.0, images/offerfiles-kernel). Same
contract source on both sides, two compilers, one deliberate split — because each side's
generated bindings are version-checked against ITS OWN compact-runtime at import time
(0.16.0 here, 0.15.0 there). Conflating them is what these two separate entries prevent.
THE RESIDUAL RISK THIS SPLIT CARRIES, stated rather than discovered: the contract is
DEPLOYED by the kernel from a 0.30.0 compile, while the browser proves against ZK assets
the kernel serves from that same 0.30.0 compile (GET /keys/*, /zkir/* — the browser's own
compiled keys are never used; only managed/contract/index.js is). So the browser's 0.31.0
bindings drive 0.30.0 proving artifacts. P3's browser mint / offer create / offer take are
the measurement that settles it; on a verifier-key rejection the fallback is Q9 option D.
midnightntwrk/compact (repo id 967499978) and LFDT-Minokawa/compact (id 1115336329) both
publish this tag, and for compactc-v0.31.0 the assets are BYTE-IDENTICAL: same sha256 and
same sizes on both Linux triples (LFDT asset ids 408401806 / 408401804, verified
2026-09-01). midnightntwrk is recorded because it is where the `compact` toolchain manager
itself is published — so it is what `compact update <v>` resolves against — and because
the kernel image already pins there; one fewer distinct upstream in the stack.
The same release also ships aarch64-darwin and x86_64-darwin zips. Those must never enter
a Linux build stage, which is why forbiddenAssetSubstrings is applied to toolchain assets
and asserted again in the Dockerfile.

proofData.reason: Proof data is architecture-neutral and belongs in one persistent volume, not embedded in an OCI layer and not fetched independently per service. The 2.x sibling populates that volume from a hash-verified immutable warehouse GENERATION, but that generation is Ledger-9 specific (SRS K0-K19 + ledger-static-noarch-9.0.0) and no equivalent v8 generation exists today. So the volume is filled by a pre-warm one-shot instead: it pays the srs.midnight.network fetch once, before up.sh reports ready, rather than during the first browser mint mid-demo.
proofData.integrityCaveat: CORRECTED AT P1/T1.3 AFTER MEASUREMENT — the earlier text here read 'these are not offline-verified bytes; the pre-warm trusts srs.midnight.network at fetch time'. That was wrong in BOTH directions and is replaced by what was actually observed. (1) The proof-server binary HASH-VERIFIES everything it downloads, SRS public parameters included: it logs 'this is not a trusted service, the data will be verified' and then 'verified correct' for every payload, against expected hashes compiled into ledger-8.1.0. So the warmed bytes are cryptographically checked, and the trust root is this repository's digest-pinned official image rather than a committed manifest — weaker than the 2.x audited generation's reviewable hash list, but very far from 'fetch-time trust'. (2) The corresponding real hazard is the opposite of the one previously recorded: a pre-warm that fetched payloads ITSELF (curl, wget) would write bytes NOTHING verifies, because the server only verifies on download and never re-checks a file it finds already present. Pre-filling this volume by URL would therefore REMOVE a property the stack has today. That is precisely why the warm one-shot runs the official proof-server binary against the volume instead of downloading anything of its own.

integrityMeasurement.coverageGap: The binary fetches only its startup working set. A contract-sized circuit needing a larger SRS k (k16+) is NOT warmed, and because the reader mounts this volume read-only that is an EROFS failure at prove time rather than a slow prove — measured: a proof server on an empty read-only MIDNIGHT_PP exits 1 with `Os { code: 30, kind: ReadOnlyFilesystem }`. Which k the offer-files contract needs cannot be known until a contract exists (P2/P3). Tracked as open question Q11.

supersededBy.note: The user is preparing an audited v8 proof-data mirror/generation in parallel. When it lands, its initializer replaces this one-shot as a drop-in WRITER OF THE SAME VOLUME, so no consumer changes. At that point `generation` becomes a 64-hex content digest and `decision` becomes warehouse-data-generation; the verifier enforces that pairing in both directions so a half-migration cannot pass.
